items.hook: In the developing human brain, DNA methylation keeps changing after gene activity has settled

readout.label: Single nuclei profiled from 40 brain specimens

items.summary: The authors measured gene expression, chromatin accessibility and DNA methylation together in each cell nucleus, from fetal stages to adolescence. Methylation kept remodeling after the main shifts in expression and accessibility, and it added information on where psychiatric risk variants act. The data come from 40 specimens, so ages and brain regions are sparsely covered.
items.title: Tri-Modal Single-Cell Atlas of Developing Human Brain

items.hook: Barcoding ribosomal DNA let researchers assemble all 18 nucleolar organizer regions of a human cell line

readout.label: Total rDNA units across 18 NORs in K562 cells

items.summary: These repeat-rich regions are the last parts of the human genome never fully assembled. The team used prime editing to insert short barcodes into nearly all rDNA units in K562 cells, then used ultra-long reads to assemble each region and count its copies (5 to 43 each). They also linked methylation to transcription for single units. It covers one cancer cell line, not a typical genome.
items.title: Saturation barcoding of ribosomal DNA resolves the nucleolar organizer regions of the human genome

items.hook: Down syndrome lymph nodes have few germinal centers, which may explain faulty antibody maturation
items.summary: People with Down syndrome have both more autoimmunity and weaker immunity. Infant lymph nodes showed far fewer germinal centers and fewer supporting stromal cells, and adult memory B cells carried fewer mutations and more of an autoreactivity-linked gene. The link from lymph node structure to the B cell changes is inferred, and sample sizes are not stated in the abstract.
items.title: Dysregulated B Cell Education Drives Autoimmunity and Immunodeficiency in Down Syndrome

items.hook: Blocking acetylcholine disrupted human hippocampal theta at retrieval without hurting memory
items.summary: Patients with implanted brain electrodes received scopolamine, which blocks acetylcholine receptors, during a memory task. Dosing at encoding disrupted slow theta waves and impaired recollection, but dosing only at retrieval disrupted theta with no memory loss. That suggests slow theta reflects encoding, not retrieval. The participants are neurosurgical patients, so results may not generalize.
items.title: Cholinergic blockade reveals a role for human hippocampal theta in memory encoding but not retrieval.

items.hook: Ewing sarcoma tumors contain several coexisting gene-regulation programs, even within a single tumor
items.summary: Ewing sarcoma is driven by one fusion protein, yet patient outcomes vary. Profiling RNA and chromatin accessibility in the same single cells, the authors found distinct regulatory modules in cell lines, one shifted by TGF-beta, and saw them mixed unevenly in patient tumors. The clinical link is only suggested, since outcomes were not tested directly.
items.title: Multimodal single-cell analyses reveal distinct fusion-regulated transcriptional programs in Ewing sarcoma.

items.hook: Feeding yeast ATP through an imported transporter extended their replicative lifespan
items.summary: Yeast cells were given a parasite ATP transporter, letting the authors set internal ATP independently of the cell's own supply. Low ATP shortened lifespan and added ATP extended it, and plain extracellular ATP also helped normal cells. The findings are in budding yeast, so whether ATP regulates aging in animals is untested.
items.title: Engineering ATP import in yeast uncovers a synthetic route to extend cellular lifespan.

items.hook: Every graph of uncountable edge-connectivity kappa contains a kappa-regular tree with an apex as a minor
items.summary: In graph theory, a minor is a structure left after deleting and contracting parts of a graph. The authors prove that every graph that stays connected after removing fewer than kappa edges, for uncountable kappa, contains a kappa-regular tree joined to one extra vertex. This extends a countable-case result of Kurkofka. It is a pure existence theorem for infinite graphs.
items.title: The unavoidable minor in graphs of uncountable edge-connectivity

items.hook: A conjectured edge-coloring formula for odd-fold graph covers fails, and the Petersen graph breaks it.
items.hook_turn: and the Petersen graph breaks it.
items.summary: The authors prove a sharp upper bound on the fewest colors needed to edge-color an odd-fold cover of a graph. They build counterexamples from cubic graphs, including the Petersen graph, to a published conjecture, and give polynomial-time algorithms. The results cover odd fold numbers only.
items.title: Edge-coloring spectra of odd-fold graph covers and counterexamples to a conjecture

items.hook: One-shot channel simulation costs I + log I + a constant bits, and that constant is proved optimal.
items.summary: The paper proves a tight bound on the entropy left over when one party simulates a channel using shared randomness, with the third-order constant shown unimprovable. It also shows the Poisson functional representation is within a constant gap of optimal. The result is theoretical and concerns the one-shot setting, with no implementation.
items.title: The Optimal Constant for One-Shot Channel Simulation and Strong Functional Representation Lemma

items.hook: Every connected vertex-transitive graph with a prime-power number of vertices has a Hamiltonian cycle.
items.summary: A vertex-transitive graph looks the same from every vertex, and the authors show that when its vertex count is a prime power (at least 3), a cycle visiting every vertex exactly once always exists. They extend Witte's 1986 theorem on Cayley digraphs of p-groups. It covers only prime-power orders, so the general question stays open.
items.title: Hamilton cycles in vertex-transitive graphs of prime-power order

items.hook: Learning a fermionic Gaussian state one copy at a time takes order m^3/eps^2 samples, and no fewer.
items.summary: For fermionic Gaussian states on m modes, single-copy measurements need and suffice with about m^3/epsilon^2 copies, versus m^2/epsilon^2 for collective measurements. The authors also fill in many entries of the sample-complexity table for bosonic and block-measurement cases. These are theoretical bounds, and the lower bound holds only for small epsilon.
items.title: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements

items.hook: In-context learning that looks like generalizing is really underfit memorization, and kernels show it.
items.summary: Studying kernel machines on an in-context linear regression task, the authors find that more data makes them learn higher-degree parts of the memorizing solution, so they generalize first and then drift into memorization. This implies feature learning is not needed for this behavior. Transformer experiments agree, but the theory is shown only for one task.
items.title: You Don't Need Feature Learning to Do In-Context Learning

items.hook: The saddle-shaped Allen-Cahn solution in even dimensions 8 and up is a global minimizer.
items.summary: The authors prove that the Cabre-Terra saddle solution of the Allen-Cahn equation in dimension 2m, for m at least 4, minimizes energy globally. Up to sign it is the only minimizer whose nodal set approaches the Simons cone with faster-than-Hardt-Simon decay. The result is specific to these even dimensions.
items.title: A uniqueness theorem for Allen--Cahn global minimizers asymptotic to the Simons cone

items.hook: A plasma wakefield compresses electron bunches, driving a free electron laser with far stronger pulses.
items.summary: The team used a plasma wakefield to chirp and compress a relativistic electron bunch without the usual loss of beam quality. The short bunch drove single-microbunch free electron lasing at optical wavelengths in a meter-scale undulator, with radiation pulses about four orders of magnitude more energetic than an earlier plasma-driven demonstration. It is one facility's demonstration, not yet a routine tool.
items.title: Compact plasma-based extreme compression of relativistic electron beams

items.hook: Every finite quotient of a finite-volume Kleinian group is realized by a surface subgroup.
items.summary: Given any surjection from a finite-covolume Kleinian group onto a finite group, the authors build a surface subgroup that still maps onto it. So surface subgroups are dense in the profinite topology. They use this to get new atoroidal surface bundles with signature zero. The result is a pure existence proof, with no explicit construction of the subgroups.
items.title: Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients

items.hook: A matrix whose numerical range has constant width must have a disk as its numerical range.
items.summary: The author proves a conjecture of Chien, Nakazato, and Meng that a finite complex matrix with constant-width numerical range has a disk-shaped range. The argument uses a common factor of the characteristic polynomials of a Hermitian pencil and its translate, which forces the extreme eigenvalue to be a first harmonic. It applies to finite matrices only.
items.title: A proof of the constant-width numerical range conjecture

items.hook: Sphere-packing bounds rule out over half the candidate K3 surface Weil polynomials over F2
items.hook_turn: rule out over half the candidate K3 surface Weil polynomials over F2

readout.label: Candidate Weil polynomials ruled out over F2

items.summary: The authors derive new necessary conditions on the zeta-function numerators (Weil polynomials) of K3 surfaces over finite fields. They compare the Artin-Tate formula over extensions and apply known lattice sphere-packing bounds to get lower bounds on special values. Applied to Kedlaya and Sutherland's candidate list over the field with 2 elements, the conditions eliminate over 50%. It only excludes candidates; it does not show the rest occur.
items.title: A cyclotomic Artin-Tate formula and sphere packing for K3 surfaces

items.hook: Twisting spacetime light lattices yields 3D moire patterns of knotted light called hopfion bags
items.hook_turn: yields 3D moire patterns of knotted light called hopfion bags
items.summary: The work builds 3D moire superlattices by twisting spatiotemporal optical lattices, producing hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals and nested hopfion superlattices. Tuning the interference polarization textures switches between these states and sets their topological numbers. The abstract does not say how much is measured versus simulated, and the information-encoding use is only proposed.
items.title: Hopfion Superlattices in 3D Twisted Moir\'e Light Fields

items.hook: The largest sunflower-free family of triples with 4 petals has span 39, cutting a bound from 162 to 130
items.summary: A sunflower-free system is a family of sets with no r sets sharing a common core and otherwise disjoint. The author constructs the largest such system of 3-element sets with no 4-flower in which every ground element is used, showing the maximum span is 39. This lowers the upper bound f(3,4) from the Erdos-Rado 162 to 130. The result covers only the single case k=3, r=4.
items.title: The Largest Ground Set for Sunflower-Free Systems

items.hook: Transit timing of hot Jupiter TOI-2109 b hints at an unseen companion of 0.70 Jupiter masses
items.hook_turn: hints at an unseen companion of 0.70 Jupiter masses

readout.label: Amplitude of periodic transit timing signal

items.summary: Using 87 transits over two decades, the team tested five timing models and found no significant orbital decay. A periodic timing signal of about 44 seconds is best fit by a non-transiting planet near a 7:3 resonance. The preference over a simple sinusoid is modest (BIC difference 4.95), so the companion is a candidate, not a confirmed planet.
items.title: A Possible Non-Transiting Companion in the TOI-2109 System Supported by Transit Timing Variations

items.hook: In theory, altermagnetism gives a topological insulator film a Hall edge channel without net magnetization
items.hook_turn: gives a topological insulator film a Hall edge channel without net magnetization
items.summary: The authors propose getting the quantum anomalous Hall effect from altermagnetic exchange on a weak topological insulator thin film, instead of ferromagnetism or magnetic doping. Altermagnetism gaps one Dirac cone while surface hybridization gaps the other, giving Chern number 1 and one chiral edge channel. This is shown only in a minimal model and slab calculations, with no experiment.
items.title: Magnetization-free quantum anomalous Hall effect in altermagnetic weak topological insulators

items.hook: Shocked gas in supernova remnant W49B points to cosmic-ray ionization thousands of times the Galactic norm
items.hook_turn: points to cosmic-ray ionization thousands of times the Galactic norm
items.summary: ALMA and APEX observations of HCO+ and CO toward W49B show twelve broad-line regions where the remnant is hitting molecular clouds. The high HCO+/CO abundance ratios need cosmic-ray ionization rates 3 to 4 orders of magnitude above the standard Galactic level. That rate is inferred from chemical modeling of a few regions, so it depends on the model assumptions.
items.title: Molecular signatures of shocked gas and enhanced cosmic-ray ionization in supernova remnant W49B revealed by ALMA

items.hook: Cube projections have maximal entropy along equal-coordinate directions in every dimension from 150 up
items.summary: The paper proves that among one-dimensional projections of a uniform cube distribution, differential entropy is largest in directions whose coordinates have equal magnitude. This confirms a conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar and Tkocz, but only for dimensions n of at least 150. Smaller dimensions remain open.
items.title: Entropy maximization for cube projections

items.hook: Covering the triangular lattice with non-overlapping unit disks is not monotone in the point spacing
items.hook_turn: is not monotone in the point spacing
items.summary: The authors determine exactly, as fifteen intervals of spacing, where a triangular lattice cannot be covered by unit disks with disjoint interiors, showing coverability is not monotone. At the edge spacings 2/sqrt(k), coverage is possible exactly when k is an Eisenstein norm. They also give two new hexagonal coverings and bound the smallest coverable spacing between 2/sqrt(55) and 1/sqrt(13). The exact minimum is still unknown.
items.title: Covering the Triangular Lattice with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks

items.hook: A simple online matching algorithm beats the one-half barrier at 0.5445 with random edge arrivals
items.hook_turn: beats the one-half barrier at 0.5445 with random edge arrivals
items.summary: In online matching, edges arrive at random times and each must be accepted or rejected immediately. A three-phase algorithm that deliberately rejects some early edges reaches ratio 0.5445 on general graphs and 0.5535 on triangle-free ones, improving a guarantee only slightly above 1/2 that stood nearly a decade. A separate upper bound shows no algorithm can exceed about 0.70, so a gap remains.
items.title: Improved Bounds for Online Matching with Random Edge Arrivals

items.hook: The textbook Greedy+Singleton knapsack heuristic has worst-case ratio exactly 0.42944
items.summary: The paper pins down the worst-case ratio of the standard heuristic for monotone submodular maximization under a knapsack constraint, closing a gap between 0.427 and 0.42945. The proof combines analytic bounds, interval-arithmetic checks and branch-and-bound, with hand-checkable bad instances. It also shows Wolsey's bound is tight for the stop-early variant. Parts of the proof rely on computer verification.
items.title: Greedy+Singleton for knapsack-constrained monotone submodular maximization has approximation ratio exactly $\beta^\star \approx 0.42944$

items.hook: A superconducting spin switch reveals a weak ferromagnetic RuOx layer hidden at the Nb/RuO2 interface
items.hook_turn: reveals a weak ferromagnetic RuOx layer hidden at the Nb/RuO2 interface
items.summary: In a GdN/Nb/RuO2 trilayer, the superconducting transition of Nb shifts with interface exchange-field alignment, exposing magnetism that magnetometry cannot see. The authors attribute it to a thin RuOx layer formed when Nb pulls oxygen from RuO2, acting as a weak, magnetically hard ferromagnet. The layer's origin is an interpretation, and the probe works only at low temperature.
items.title: Hidden interfacial magnetism in RuO$_2$ heterostructures revealed by a superconducting spin switch

items.hook: Graphic TSP tours can be found within 89/64 of the lower bound, beating the long-standing 7/5

readout.label: Integrality gap bound, graphic TSP subtour LP

items.summary: The authors give a polynomial-time algorithm for graphic TSP that returns a tour at most 89/64 times the subtour relaxation value, improving the 7/5 of Sebo and Vygen. They optimize a non-linear objective over an odd-join polytope using a new removable edge system. The gain is small, and the ratio is for graphic instances only, not general TSP.
items.title: Approximating graphic TSP by b-matchings

items.hook: A nonlinear periodic orbit maps to a topological chain whose winding number flips at the separatrix
items.hook_turn: whose winding number flips at the separatrix
items.summary: Writing a classical orbit's Lax operator in a frequency basis gives a flat-band Su-Schrieffer-Heeger-type chain whose winding number is topological. In a symmetric double well it changes when orbits merge at the separatrix, and the edge mode's localization length diverges logarithmically. Quantized, the winding numbers sum to the Witten index. The results are analytic and cover one-degree-of-freedom systems.
items.title: Topological flat bands from nonlinear periodic motion

items.hook: Nonnegative weak tilings can satisfy condition (T1) but fail (T2), with an explicit case in Z_180
items.summary: Researchers build a general method for finding nonnegative functions on finite cyclic groups that meet the Coven-Meyerowitz condition (T1) but not (T2) while acting as a weak complement to a tile. They also show that a tile with an unsupported divisor has a dilation with such a complement, and give an explicit example in the group of order 180. The examples are not positive definite, so they leave open the positive-definite extension of the conditions.
items.title: Nonnegative weak tilings and the Coven-Meyerowitz condition (T2)

items.hook: Two transformer layers are necessary and sufficient to run depth-first search on graphs efficiently
items.summary: The paper proves that a one-layer transformer needs size growing as N squared on dense graphs to pick the next DFS child, while two layers do full DFS with N log N size. Deeper models gain an exponentially longer look-ahead horizon, and a two-layer model provably learns DFS by gradient flow. All results concern idealized transformers and curated training data, not production language models.
items.title: Transformers Provably Learn Graph Search: Training Dynamics and the Exponential Power of Depth

items.hook: The bilinear Hilbert transform is shown to satisfy a weak-type bound at exponent 2/3
items.summary: The proof covers inputs in L^p1 and L^p2 with p1 and p2 between 1 and 2 and 1/p1+1/p2=3/2. The key step is a new local supremum estimate for packet sums, used to prove the forest estimate in the time-frequency analysis. The result is a weak-type bound, a weaker conclusion than a strong bound, and it holds only for this range of exponents.
items.title: Weak $L^{2/3}$ bounds for the bilinear Hilbert transform

items.hook: A 1939 Erdős and Mahler conjecture is false. Numbers exist with infinitely many 2^a/3^b convergents.
items.hook_turn: Numbers exist with infinitely many 2^a/3^b convergents.
items.summary: The author builds, for every real tau at least 4, a Cantor set of numbers with irrationality exponent tau, each having infinitely many continued-fraction convergents of the form 2^a/3^b. This gives a counterexample to the conjecture. The construction works only for tau of 4 or more, so smaller exponents are not covered by this result.
items.title: A counterexample to the Erd\H{o}s--Mahler conjecture

items.hook: Graphs with no vertex in every triangle must have about as many triangles as their spectral radius
items.summary: The authors prove that such a graph has at least its adjacency spectral radius minus a constant in triangles, which is stronger than a conjecture of Li, Feng and Peng. They bound the sum of squared eigenvalues, use interlacing and perturbation estimates to pin down a vertex neighborhood, then count triangles with weights. The bound applies when the spectral radius exceeds the square root of the edge count.
items.title: Triangles without a common vertex

items.hook: Inverted neutrino mass ordering is disfavored at 1.9 sigma, but T2K and NOvA pull opposite ways
items.hook_turn: but T2K and NOvA pull opposite ways
items.summary: Combining JUNO and Daya Bay reactor data with muon-neutrino disappearance from NOvA, T2K, MINOS and IceCube/DeepCore, the authors find the preference comes from several small, partly opposing effects. A shift of about 3.5% in one experiment's mass splitting could reverse it, and more JUNO data alone would not push rejection past about 3 sigma. This is a global fit, so it depends on each experiment's published uncertainties and interaction modeling.
items.title: Where does the neutrino Mass Ordering preference come from?

items.hook: A transformer decoder matches slower integer-programming decoders and runs in 6.59 microseconds on an FPGA

readout.label: Decoding latency, distance-8 block on FPGA

items.summary: PRISM is a transformer decoder that uses the known locations of erasures in photonic fusion-based quantum computing. On surface, color and quantum LDPC codes up to distance 24 it matches the logical error rates of integer-programming decoders while running faster. An FPGA implementation decodes a distance-8 block in 6.59 microseconds. Benchmarks are on simulated noise, not on real photonic hardware.
items.title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time

items.hook: Starlink signals with precise orbit data gave 2.33 m horizontal accuracy (95%) in a field test
items.summary: The team extracted time-of-arrival measurements from live Starlink Ku-band downlinks and paired them with high-fidelity orbit and clock models, as if the operator supplied them. In a field campaign the 95% error bounds were 2.33 m horizontal, 3.37 m vertical and 11.19 ns in timing. The orbit and clock data were produced by the researchers, not provided by Starlink, so this is a mock of a possible future system.
items.title: Toward Pseudorange-Based PNT with Starlink: A Mock Fused LEO GNSS Implementation

items.hook: Convex tilings by one tile shape with equal neighbor counts have at most 21 neighbors per tile

readout.label: Maximum common neighbor number per tile

items.summary: The authors prove that when every tile in a convex monohedral plane tiling has the same number of neighbors, that number is at most 21. Equality holds only for a 30-30-120 degree triangle tiling similar to a central subdivision of the equilateral triangular tiling. They use boundary curvature estimates, angle counts and side-length matching, and settle an open problem from The Tiling Book.
items.title: Convex monohedral tilings: a sharp neighbor bound and rigidity in the equality case

items.hook: Two atoms at dense packing feel strong light-induced dipole-dipole forces, shifting their resonance
items.summary: The experiment prepared pairs of atoms at densities above 10^16 per cubic centimeter and probed them with light. Off-resonant light dressed the atoms with a dipole moment near 1 Debye, and the two-body Lamb shift moved the resonance, dominated by near-field dipole coupling. Earlier shifts were seen only with many atoms in the far field. The abstract reports no precise shift values or error bars.
items.title: Observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between two atoms

items.hook: Gödel's second incompleteness theorem still holds in a logic where truth is grounded evaluation.
items.summary: The paper builds Reflective Grounded Arithmetic, a system whose implication is weaker than usual, and shows Gödel's argument survives as entailments rather than implications. The second theorem is proved once for a whole class of extensions, and the proofs are machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL. A natural question, whether the inductive variant alone derives the base system's consistency, stays open, and the results apply only to these purpose-built systems.
items.title: G\"odel's Incompleteness Theorems in Grounded Arithmetic
